name: Schematic Symbol Checklist
blurb: pin types, names and electrical properties to check on a new symbol
intro: Tick what is checked on a new schematic symbol; what is still open comes back with the failure it causes. The items follow IPC-2612-1, the KiCad Library Conventions and the usual first-spin pinout mistakes; set the part kind first so only the relevant checks show.

inputs.label: Part kind
Multi-unit symbol (e.g. dual op-amp, FPGA banks)
Package has an exposed / thermal pad
Pins: Pin count equals the package pin count, NC and exposed pad included
inputs.help: A pin missing from the symbol leaves its pad unconnected in the layout, and no check will tell you.

inputs.label: Pins: Pin numbers match the datasheet for this exact package
inputs.help: The same chip has a different pinout in SOIC and QFN; a swapped number is a board respin.

inputs.label: Pins: Pin names as in the datasheet, active-low marked (~{RESET} or RESET_N)
inputs.help: Renamed pins make the schematic impossible to check against the datasheet.

inputs.label: Pins: Electrical type set on every pin (input, output, bidirectional, tri-state, passive...)
inputs.help: ERC finds undriven inputs and output conflicts only from these types; all-passive pins disable it.

inputs.label: Pins: Supply pins are Power input; regulator outputs are Power output
inputs.help: ERC then flags a rail with no source, and two sources shorted together.

inputs.label: Pins: Open-drain / open-collector outputs typed as such
inputs.help: Typed as plain outputs, shared lines (I2C, interrupts) give output-to-output ERC errors.

inputs.label: Pins: Only truly unconnected pins typed No-connect ("reserved, tie to GND" is not NC)
inputs.help: Reserved pins that must be tied get left floating when marked NC.

inputs.label: Pins: No hidden power pins (or deliberately, with the net name documented)
inputs.help: Hidden pins join a net by name: a part on another rail is silently tied to the wrong supply.

inputs.label: Pins: Repeated GND/VDD pins all present, stacked or shown on purpose
inputs.help: A GND pin left out of a stack is an unconnected pad: less current, worse thermal and EMC.

inputs.label: Pins: Exposed / thermal pad is a pin with its own number and its net (usually GND)
inputs.help: Without a pin the pad has no net: the layout leaves it unsoldered or unconnected.

inputs.label: Graphics: Pin ends on the 100 mil (2.54 mm) grid, pointing outward
inputs.help: Off-grid pin ends do not connect to wires; ERC reports them unconnected (or misses them).

inputs.label: Graphics: Inputs left, outputs right, supplies top, ground bottom; related pins grouped
inputs.help: Signal flow reads left to right; review is faster and errors show.

inputs.label: Graphics: Polarity / pin 1 visible (diode cathode, electrolytic +, pin 1 of connectors)
inputs.help: The schematic is what assembly and debug read to know the orientation.

inputs.label: Graphics: Names and numbers readable at print size, not overlapping the body or each other
inputs.help: Unreadable pin numbers slow every review and bring-up.

inputs.label: Graphics: Symbol origin at the body centre, on grid
inputs.help: Rotated or mirrored symbols stay on grid and connect.

inputs.label: Fields: Reference prefix is standard (U, R, C, L, D, Q, J, Y, F...)
inputs.help: Annotation, BOM grouping and assembly drawings rely on it (IEEE 315 / ASME Y14.44).

inputs.label: Fields: Value field holds the value or the part number
inputs.help: The BOM and the schematic print show it.

inputs.label: Fields: Footprint assigned, and its pad numbers match the pin numbers
inputs.help: The netlist connects by number: a mismatch routes signals to the wrong pads.

inputs.label: Fields: Manufacturer and MPN fields (or a link to your parts database)
inputs.help: The BOM needs an orderable part; "10k" alone is not one.

inputs.label: Fields: Ratings where they matter: voltage for capacitors, power for resistors, current for inductors
inputs.help: A right value with a wrong rating fails in the field (cap derating, resistor burn-out).

inputs.label: Fields: Datasheet link
inputs.help: Reviewers check the pinout against it.

inputs.label: Fields: Description and keywords filled in
inputs.help: The part can be found in the library search, and not duplicated.

inputs.label: Multi-unit: Each unit has its own pins; no pin in two units
inputs.help: A pin in two units is connected twice or not at all.

inputs.label: Multi-unit: Units / pins marked swappable only where they really are
inputs.help: Pin and gate swapping in layout must not swap non-equivalent pins.

inputs.label: Multi-unit: Power pins in their own unit or on every unit, as your tool expects
inputs.help: An unplaced power unit leaves the chip unpowered; ERC "missing unit" catches it only if set up.

inputs.label: Connector: Numbering matches the physical connector and its mating half
inputs.help: Plug and receptacle often number mirror-image; pin 1 of the cable is not always pin 1 of the board.

inputs.label: Connector: Shield / shell / mounting pins present as numbered pins
inputs.help: Otherwise the shield has no net and the footprint pads are orphaned.

inputs.label: Verify: Library checker passes (KiCad symbol checker, Altium component rule check)
inputs.help: Catches duplicate pin numbers, off-grid pins and empty fields for free.

inputs.label: Verify: Placed in a test sheet with typical connections: ERC clean
inputs.help: Shows at once whether the pin types make sense.

inputs.label: Verify: Pinout cross-checked against the datasheet by a second person
inputs.help: Pinout errors are the most common first-spin schematic bug; a second reader finds most.

examples.title: New QFN MCU symbol, pins and footprint done

usage: Set kind (ic, passive or conn) and the multi and ep booleans, then set each check key (p_count, p_numbers, p_types, f_fp...) to true when done. It returns progress in %, the open checks with why each matters, a per-group summary and an 'Open items' text listing what is left; a warning names the open checks that would put wrong connections on the board. Use it when creating or reviewing a library symbol.
sources: KiCad Library Conventions (KLC) S3/S4: pin grid, electrical types, hidden power pins, fields
IEEE 315 / IEC 60617 graphic symbols; ASME Y14.44 reference designators
